title: Nasdaq Gains 0.8% on Election Day as Chips Rebound; Dow Falls 0.4% on Apple
dek: The S&P 500 rose 0.4% to 7,568.92, the Nasdaq Composite added 0.8% to 25,372.01 and the Dow lost 0.4% to 51,786.72 at the close, with AMD reporting after the bell.

keyPoints: S&P 500 closed at 7,568.92, up 27.52 points or 0.4%, though most of its stocks fell (AP).
Nasdaq Composite rose 207.65 points, or 0.8%, to 25,372.01; the Dow fell 197.26 points, or 0.4%, to 51,786.72 (AP).

body:
## Close: chips lift the Nasdaq, Apple weighs on the Dow

The Nasdaq Composite rose 207.65 points, or 0.8%, to 25,372.01 on Tuesday, recouping part of Monday's loss. The S&P 500 rose 27.52 points, or 0.4%, to 7,568.92, even though most of the index's components fell. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 197.26 points, or 0.4%, to 51,786.72, with Apple the main drag. The Russell 2000 rose 0.2% to 2,812.45 (AP).

Chip stocks did most of the work. Stock Titan said the Nasdaq-100 tracking fund finished up 0.62% on the day, while the Dow tracking fund fell 0.44% (Stock Titan). Investrade noted that the semiconductor index had given back about 12% in the three days before the session, which made the rebound a relief move as much as a new trend (Investrade).

## Apple and Ibotta: one lower on margins, one higher on a beat

Apple ended down 1.90%, or about $94 billion of market value below Monday's close, after a fiscal fourth-quarter margin forecast that warned of rising memory costs (Stock Titan, AP). Apple was the largest single drag on the Dow.

Ibotta closed up 20.62% after its third-quarter revenue rose 17% to $97.8 million, above the top of its own forecast range (Stock Titan). Aehr Test Systems also ended among the top gainers after a raised sales forecast, and Stevanato Group was among the biggest decliners (Stock Titan).

This edition does not include a verified closing move for CrowdStrike. Its midday move was reported on the midday edition, and no closing figure was confirmed in the sources used here.

## Oil and Treasuries

Oil fell as traders weighed talks with Iran against renewed military activity. WTI settled at $96.09 a barrel, down 0.38%, and Brent settled at $103.60, down 1.12% (Investrade, CNBC). Both were at their lowest settlements in about a month.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.966% in afternoon trading, up more than 6 basis points, after a stronger-than-expected JOLTS report showed 7.5 million September job openings against about 7.1 million forecast (CNBC, Investrade). The 30-year yield was 5.334% (CNBC). These are intraday levels from CNBC rather than a confirmed closing yield.

## Election Day and after the bell

The midterm votes were still being counted at the close. Investors had been watching the House and Senate outcomes through the session, and the VIX stayed above 20 for most of the day (Investrade). AMD reports after the bell; that result is covered in a separate story.

## What to watch

The next scheduled economic releases are ISM services PMI and ADP employment on Wednesday, Nov. 4, and the October jobs report on Friday, Nov. 6 (Trading Economics, Investopedia).

marketImpact.summary: The Nasdaq's gain was driven by a chip rebound, while Apple's margin warning weighed on the Dow. Oil fell and yields rose on the JOLTS data. The close leaves the market waiting on the midterm results and on tonight's AMD guidance.
